# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 👏 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 👏 ☝ ☝ ☝ 👏 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 👏 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 👏 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]

I can see the bomb’s current state but cannot operate it. The display reads 0, the light is white, and the three wires are yellow, green, and blue. I am telling Blind these facts so the manual can determine the required action. The gesture sequence from Mute appears to encode grouped counts, but no encoding has been established, so I will not treat it as a definite instruction.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb shows display 0. Light is white. Wires from 1 to 3 are yellow, green, blue.")
speak(to="mute", text="I see display 0, white light, and wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. I do not know what your gesture code means.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 🫱 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 👏 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 🙌 🫱 ☝ ☝ ☝ 👏 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 🙌 🫱 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 👏 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 🫴]

The display remains 0 and the wire colours are unchanged, but the light is now purple. Blind needs the updated light colour to apply the manual’s rule. Mute’s gestures still have no established meaning to me, so I will not infer an action from them.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Update: display is still 0; light is now purple; wires remain 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue.")
speak(to="mute", text="Update: display 0, purple light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Please convey the manual's required action to Blind.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👇]

The light has changed again, now to red; display and wires are unchanged. I will report that to Blind. Mute’s two gestures were ✌ followed by 👇; since Blind cannot see gestures, I will describe them verbally rather than assume their meaning.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Update: display 0, light red, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute signaled two gestures: victory hand, then down-pointing hand.")
speak(to="mute", text="I see the light is red. I relayed your two gestures to Blind as victory hand then down-pointing hand.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👇]

The display remains 0 and the wires remain yellow, green, blue. The light has returned to white. Mute’s new gesture pair is 🤟 followed by 👇; I can only report the gesture descriptions, not infer their meaning.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Update: display 0, light white, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute signaled 🤟 (love-you hand) then 👇 (down-pointing hand).")
speak(to="mute", text="I see the light is white again. I relayed your latest gestures to Blind as love-you hand then down-pointing hand.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👇]

The display and wires are unchanged, while the light is purple again. Mute’s latest gesture pair is ☝ followed by 👇. I will describe both gestures to Blind so Blind can combine them with the manual’s instructions.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Update: display 0, light purple, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute signaled a raised index finger, then a down-pointing index finger.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👇]

The display remains 0 and the wires remain yellow, green, blue. The light is now red. Mute again sent ☝ followed by 👇; I will pass both the current bomb state and the gesture descriptions to Blind, who can use the manual to interpret them.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Update: display 0, light red, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute signaled a raised index finger, then a down-pointing index finger.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👇]

The display remains 0 and the wires remain yellow, green, blue; the light is white again. Mute’s latest signal is ✌ followed by 👇, matching the pair from Turn 3. I will pass the exact gesture descriptions and current bomb state to Blind.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Turn 7: display 0, light white, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute signaled ✌ (victory hand) followed by 👇 (down-pointing hand), same pair as Turn 3.")
```
